q: 1. The total cost versus time curve is ............
explain: The total cost curve is U-shaped because it is the sum of direct costs (which decrease with more time) and indirect costs (which increase over time).

q: 2. Crashing to the project means ............
options: reducing the time of completion by spending more resources
reducing the cost of project by delaying the time of completion
reducing the project size to save the resources
explain: Project crashing is the technique of adding extra resources (labor, overtime, equipment) to shorten the duration of critical activities.

q: 3. A hand-held air-operated percussion type drill used for drilling down holes is ............
explain: A jack hammer is a portable, hand-held pneumatic tool used primarily for vertical or down-hole drilling in rock or concrete.

q: 4. A drill most suitable for drilling down, horizontal, or up holes is ............
explain: A drifter is a heavy-duty rock drill mounted on a support (like a jumbo or frame) that can efficiently drill in various orientations: up, down, or horizontal.

q: 5. When the time of earliest finish and the latest finish are equal in an operation, the operation is called ............
explain: If EF = LF, the total float is zero. Activities with zero float are termed 'Critical' because any delay in them will delay the entire project.

q: 6. A drawback of the bar chart is that ............
options: all the activity are independent of each other
it is difficult to judge whether an activity is completed or not
the sequence of activity is not clearly defined
explain: Gantt charts (bar charts) lack interdependency details, don't easily show the critical path, and can make it difficult to monitor precise progress in complex projects.

q: 7. Select the incorrect statement ............
options: a critical path always begins at the very first event
a critical path always terminates at the last event
critical activities control the project duration
critical activity is the one for which free float is zero
explain: While a critical activity has a Total Float of zero, having a Free Float of zero is not the defining characteristic, as non-critical activities can also have zero free float.

q: 8. Select the incorrect statements ............
options: its latest start time and earliest start time for its successor activity
its latest start time and earliest starts time
its latest finish time and earliest starts time for its successor activity
its earliest finish time and latest time for its successor activity
explain: The latest start time of an activity is not directly equated to the earliest start time of its successor; these values depend on activity duration and float.

q: 9. Free float is the ............
explain: Free float is the portion of total float that can be used without affecting the early start of the immediately following successor activity.

q: 10. Critical path is ............
options: shortest path for the earliest completion of the project
longest path of the network from the first event to the last event
ideal path by preceding along which the project can be completed as per the schedule
the path which takes into account the completion of all the parallel activities
explain: The critical path is the specific sequence of activities that represents the minimum time required to complete the project as scheduled.

q: 11. Resource smoothening means ............
options: adjustment of resources to have the least variations
complete revamping of resources to suit the requirement
optimisation and economical utilisation of resources
explain: Resource smoothing is a technique used to level the peaks and valleys of resource demand within the limits of the project's float.

q: 12. When all the paths are arranged according to the descending order of the float, the path which is next to critical path is known as ............
explain: A 'Semi-critical' or 'Sub-critical' path is a path that has a very low amount of float and can easily become a critical path if minor delays occur.

q: 13. The time by which the completion of an activity can be delayed without affecting the start of succeeding activities is called ............
explain: Free Float is the amount of time that an activity can be delayed without delaying the Earliest Start (ES) of any successor.

q: 14. Fulkerson's rule is used for numbering the ............
explain: Fulkerson's Rule provides a systematic procedure for numbering events (nodes) in a project network diagram in a logical order.

q: 15. The probability distribution taken to represent the completion time in P.E.R.T. analysis is ............
explain: PERT assumes that the duration of an activity follows a Beta Distribution, which accounts for the asymmetry between optimistic and pessimistic times.

q: 16. According to Beta distribution, the standard deviation of the time of completion is given by ............
explain: Standard deviation ($σ$) in PERT is calculated as $(t_p - t_o) / 6$, where $t_p$ is pessimistic time and $t_o$ is optimistic time.

q: 17. The optimistic, most likely and pessimistic time estimates of an activity are 5, 10, 21 days, what are the expected time and standard deviation?
explain: Expected time $T_e = (t_o + 4t_m + t_p)/6 = (5 + 40 + 21)/6 = 11$. Standard deviation $σ = (21-5)/6 = 2.67$.

q: 18. Cost-benefit studies are essential to ............
options: assess the total cost of the work
ascertain the relevant escalation in prices
evaluate the viability and worthwhileness of taking up the project
explain: A Cost-Benefit Analysis (CBA) is a financial assessment tool used to determine if the benefits of a project outweigh the costs before starting.

q: 19. Higher standard deviations means ............
explain: In statistics and PERT, a higher standard deviation indicates a wider range of possible outcomes, which directly corresponds to higher risk and uncertainty.

q: 20. Slack is given as the difference between ............
options: latest allowable time and earliest expected time
latest allowable time and the pessimistic time estimate
earliest expected time and latest allowable time
final event time and initial event time
explain: Event Slack = Latest Allowable Time ($T_L$) - Earliest Expected Time ($T_E$).

q: 21. For all the events along the critical path, the slack is ............
explain: By definition, events on the critical path have the least amount of flexibility, meaning their slack is zero (or the minimum constant value in the network).

q: 22. A dummy activity in a network ............
options: is represented by a dotted line
does not consume time or resources
explain: Dummies are artificial activities shown with dashed arrows to represent logical dependencies without adding time or cost to the project.

q: 23. In the critical path of construction planning, free float can be ............
explain: Free float is a subset of Total Float, and mathematically, Free Float is always greater than or equal to Independent Float ($TF ≥ FF ≥ IF$).

q: 24. Which of the following is a dummy activity?
options: awaiting the arrivals of concrete material
explain: Wait times or administrative dependencies that don't involve active labor or machine work are modeled as dummies to maintain network logic.

q: 25. The resources in a construction project are made up of ............
options: plant equipment and machinery required for the project
construction material such as cement, bricks, steel etc
explain: The 4 M's of construction resources are Men (Manpower), Materials, Machinery (Plant), and Money.

q: 26. Technical planning is carried out for the ............
explain: Technical planning bridges the gap between the concept and execution by producing the precise drawings and cost calculations (estimates) needed.

q: 27. For the preparation of a construction schedule, the data required is ............
explain: To build a schedule, you must know what needs to be done (activities), how they are grouped (operations), and how fast they can be done (labor productivity).

q: 28. Bottom dump wagons are not suitable for ............
explain: Wet clay is sticky and cohesive; it tends to bridge or get stuck in the discharge gates of a bottom dump wagon.

q: 29. Variance is ............
options: sum of time duration for various job / number of jobs
difference between number under consideration and mean time
mean of square root of mean of squared deviation
square root of mean of squared deviations
explain: In the context of PERT, variance ($σ^2$) is the square of the standard deviation, representing the mean of the squared deviations from the expected time.

q: 30. If for a activity optimistic time is 1 day pessimistic times is 8 days and most likely time is 3 days then the expected time is ............
31. Standard deviation when optimistic time and earliest expected time ............
explain: Standard Deviation $σ = (t_p - t_o) / 6$. For the values in Q66: $(8 - 1) / 6 = 1.167$.

options: difference of lastest allowable time and earliest expected time
earliest expected time - lastest allowable time
explain: Slack specifically refers to events (nodes) and is calculated as $T_L - T_E$.

q: 33. Pick up the correct statement from the following ............
options: in a network activities are represented by arrows and events are circled
events into which a number of activities enter and from which one or several activities emerge are called the merge nodes
events into which one or several activities enter and from which a number of emerging activities are generated are called burst nodes
explain: These are the fundamental definitions of network components (arrows/nodes) and node types (merge/burst).

q: 34. Interfering float is the difference between ............
explain: Interfering Float ($IF = TF - FF$) is equal to the head event slack.

q: 35. Negative float for any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: An activity with negative float is 'Super-critical' because it is already behind the required completion date.

q: 36. Zero float any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: Zero float indicates a 'Critical' activity; any delay will immediately impact the project finish date.

q: 37. Positive float for any activity means that the activity is ............
explain: Positive float indicates a 'Sub-critical' or non-critical activity with some flexibility in its timing.

q: 38. Total project cost ............
options: initially reduces and then increases with increase in time
initially increases and then reduces with increase in time
explain: Total cost follows a U-curve: as time increases, direct costs drop but indirect costs rise, leading to a minimum point.

q: 39. Identify the odd man out ............
explain: 'Design completed' is an Event (a point in time), whereas the others are Activities (actions that consume time).

q: 40. An important principle in drawing a network is ............
options: no activity can start until all the previous activities in the same chain are completed
parallel activities should begin and end at the same time
between two events there should not be more than two activities
the number of dummy activities in a network should not exceed 4
explain: This is the principle of logical precedence; a successor cannot begin until its predecessors are finished.

q: 41. A dummy activity ............
options: has no tail event but only a head event
has only head event but tail event
does not require any resources or any time
has no bearing on the network and can appear anywhere
explain: Dummies are logical connectors only; they are 'zero-time' and 'zero-resource' activities.

q: 42. Negative slack occurs ............
options: when lastest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
when events sticks to their schedule
explain: Negative slack indicates the project is behind schedule, often caused by inadequate resources or delays.

q: 43. Critical path ............
explain: The critical path is the longest sequence of activities, which means it has the least (minimum) amount of slack/float.

options: the earliest time by which an activity may commence
lastest time by which an activity can be delayed without hapering the completion of the project
lastest allowable time - earliest expected time
time available time required for an activity
explain: Float is the difference between the time available for an activity and the time required ($T_L - T_E$).

q: 45. Latest starts of an activity is always ............
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: The Latest Start ($LS$) must occur at or after the latest possible completion of the previous activity to maintain logic.

q: 46. An activity of the project is graphically represented by ............ on the network
explain: In Activity-on-Arrow (AOA) diagrams, arrows represent tasks (activities).

q: 47. Which of the following statement is correct about the network diagram?
options: the events are represented graphically by circles or nodes at the beginning and the end of activity by arrows
the tail end of the arrow represents the start of the activity
the head of the arrow represents the end of an activity
explain: These are the standard conventions for drawing AOA (Activity-on-Arrow) network diagrams.

q: 48. If the completion time for a particular project is 20 weeks and its earliest expected time is 22 weeks, then the slack time for the project is ............
explain: Slack = $T_L - T_E$. Here $20 - 22 = -2$ weeks.

q: 49. Interfering float is the difference between ............
explain: Interfering float is defined as $TF - FF$; it represents the part of the total float that, if used, consumes the slack of a successor event.

q: 50. Which of the following is not an excavating equipment?
explain: A Scraper is primarily an earth-moving (hauling and spreading) machine, whereas the others are dedicated excavators.
